paragraphs.text: Reference is invited to the record-keeping obligations of banks under the anti-money laundering framework. This circular specifies the records of transactions and customer identification to be maintained, the period for which such records must be retained, and the manner in which records shall be made available to competent authorities.

Records of transactions to be maintained by banks shall include the nature of the transaction, the amount and currency, the date of the transaction and the parties to the transaction, so as to permit reconstruction of individual transactions if required as evidence.

The retention period for records of transactions shall be 5 years from the date of the transaction: banks shall preserve all necessary records of transactions between the bank and the customer for at least 5 years from the date of the transaction.

The retention period for identification records shall be 5 years after the business relationship has ended: banks shall preserve records of customer identification, account files and business correspondence for at least 5 years after the business relationship is ended or the account is closed, whichever is later.

Retrieval of records: records maintained by banks shall be held in a hard or soft format that allows them to be retrieved and furnished to the Financial Intelligence Unit or other competent authorities within three working days of a request.

Where an investigation or a Suspicious Transaction Report relating to a customer is pending, the records of that customer shall be retained until the bank is informed that the matter is closed, even if the retention period has expired. The record retention provisions of circular GZ-AML-2020-01 shall be effective from April 1, 2020.
